reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Uncontrolled Graves disease (out of methimazole, SSKI never filled, AM beta blocker missed) with a substernal goiter narrowing the trachea to 6 mm, orthopnea, and a sister with a high fever under anesthesia.

asa.rationale: Uncontrolled thyrotoxicosis with AF RVR and a critical fixed upper airway obstruction.

decision.recommendation: postpone elective surgery and optimize, unless the airway forces urgency
decision.rationale: FT4 3.8 and FT3 9.6, HR 124 AF, T 37.9: thyroid storm risk is high. Endocrinology advised deferring until euthyroid. If worsening airway compression forces surgery, prepare full storm treatment and a critical airway plan.

redFlags.evidence: TSH under 0.01, FT4 3.8 (rising), FT3 9.6, HR 124 AF, T 37.9, tremor; methimazole ran out 2 weeks ago; SSKI never filled; AM propranolol not taken.
redFlags.implication: Thyroid storm during or after surgery.
redFlags.action: Postpone and optimize: thionamide, beta blockade (give propranolol now), iodine after thionamide, steroids; storm treatment ready if proceeding.

redFlags.finding: Critical tracheal compression from substernal goiter
redFlags.evidence: CT: trachea narrowed to 6 mm at thoracic inlet, deviated; goiter to the aortic arch; flow volume loop fixed obstruction; orthopnea, sleeps upright.
redFlags.implication: Complete airway obstruction possible at induction or with paralysis; the NIM tube may not pass.
redFlags.action: Awake fiberoptic intubation or inhalation induction preserving spontaneous ventilation, small tubes ready, rigid bronchoscopy and ECMO or CPB standby, thoracic surgery present, no paralysis before the airway is secured.

redFlags.finding: Family history suggestive of malignant hyperthermia
redFlags.evidence: PAT note: sister had a high fever under anesthesia, details unknown.
redFlags.implication: Treat as MH susceptible until clarified; thyroid storm and MH can look alike.
redFlags.action: Trigger free anesthetic (TIVA, no succinylcholine, no volatiles), dantrolene available, clarify with the sister's records.

redFlags.evidence: Voice change 3 months; flexible laryngoscopy not ordered.
redFlags.implication: Baseline vocal cord palsy changes risk of bilateral palsy after surgery.

redFlags.evidence: HR 112 to 124 AF; apixaban held 48 h.
redFlags.action: Beta blockade, rate control before induction.

redFlags.evidence: Surgeon requests NIM tube and no long acting relaxant after intubation.
redFlags.implication: Limits paralysis; tube size vs 6 mm trachea.
redFlags.action: Plan relaxant strategy and confirm a tube size that passes.

planItems.item: Awake fiberoptic or spontaneous ventilation induction; small ETT and NIM size check
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
Cuff leak and cord assessment before extubation; extubation over an exchange catheter
Step down: watch hematoma, hypocalcemia, storm

boothComplications.why: Possible MH susceptibility if triggers are used
Airway surgery and recurrent laryngeal nerve risk at emergence
